clue.text: Comment on Matthew's successor

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
in the New Testament the Gospel of Mark follows the Gospel of Matthew

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on who followed Matthew in a job or role.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew looks like a person with a successor in office; it is the order of the Gospels, where Mark comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a passing observation, the same thing as a comment.

clue.text: As far as I can see, story mostly is on the level

parts.words: As far as I can see
parts.note: the horizon is the furthest line the eye can reach

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word tale, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A speaker vouches that, as far as they can tell, the story is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the level' reads as honest, but here it means flat. 'Mostly' drops the E of TALE, leaving TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horizontal lies flat, parallel to the ground, that is, level.

clue.text: Resistance worker put off accepting death

indicators.note: accepting means the delaying word takes the word for death inside it

parts.note: to defer is to postpone or put off
an end is a death, as in 'came to a sticky end'

explanation.surface: A member of the Resistance postpones facing death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance worker' suggests a wartime partisan; it simply means anyone who resists an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is one who holds out against attack, working to resist it.

clue.text: Get ambassador to make tea? Language!

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
to brew is to make tea

explanation.surface: Someone tells the ambassador to make the tea, provoking a cry of 'Language!' at the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language!' looks like a rebuke for rudeness; it is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew is the tongue of Israel and of the Jewish scriptures.

clue.text: Break point in game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the interval between the two halves of a match
second meaning: the moment in a game when half the time has passed

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tennis break point; the two halves are two senses of the same interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Halftime is the pause midway through a football or rugby match, and also that exact moment of the game.

clue.text: Speaking, forbade reflective girl to wear this?

definitions.text: Speaking, forbade reflective girl to wear this?

indicators.note: speaking means the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: banned means forbade; said aloud it is the word band

indicators.note: reflective means the name reads the same in a mirror, backwards and forwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is stopped from wearing something, and the clue asks what the forbidden item was.
explanation.walkthrough: BAND sounds like 'banned'; ANNA is a palindrome, hence 'reflective'. The whole clue then hints at a headscarf a girl might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large coloured kerchief worn on the head or neck, something a girl might put on.

clue.text: Make surgeon fall ill and have a perfect fit

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
a vet is an animal surgeon
to ail is to be or fall ill

explanation.surface: Something makes a surgeon sick, yet everything else fits perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a tight interlocking woodworking joint, so to dovetail is to fit together exactly.

clue.text: A spin out in this?

indicators.note: spin means the letters of out are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: The clue asks whether you would go out for a spin in this.
explanation.walkthrough: A is given as written; 'spin' then rearranges OUT to UTO. Read whole, a spin out is a drive in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An auto is a car, the vehicle you would take out for a spin.

clue.text: Fat boy eating last of burger

indicators.note: eating means the boy takes the letter inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of burger is taken

parts.note: the last letter of burger

explanation.surface: An overweight boy is finishing off a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' takes R, the final letter of burger, and 'eating' puts it inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat rendered for cooking, a solid fat.

clue.text: Secure golden carriage

parts.note: to land is to secure, as in land a deal or a fish
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a gilded coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding hood.

clue.text: Female priest, a senior manager

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A woman priest who also serves as a top executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on a company board, one of its most senior executives.

clue.text: History of disc — part of it first

indicators.note: first means the piece for part of the disc goes before the disc

parts.note: a track is one song or section of a record
a record is a disc

explanation.surface: A historian looks at the story of a disc, beginning with one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A track record is a person's past performance, their history of achievement.

clue.text: The look on the face of one on holding up a train?

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower pieces hold up the train, sitting beneath it

parts.note: an express is a fast train
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It asks what look appears on the face of a robber holding up a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' suggests a train robbery; in a down entry it means the later pieces sit beneath the train and support it.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression is the look a face wears, showing feeling.

clue.text: Find pole to agitate frogs, for example

indicators.note: to agitate is to stir up, so the letters of find pole are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to find a pole and stir the frogs about.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs are among the creatures living in and around ponds, an example of pond life.

clue.text: Prize rams in new enterprises

parts.note: star means prize or best, as in star pupil
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Prize-winning rams feature in new farming ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a northern British word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Start-ups are newly founded businesses, fresh enterprises.

clue.text: What may catch trespassers, some returning to island

indicators.note: to means the turned piece is attached to the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Man, often just Man in crosswords

indicators.note: returning means the word for some goes back, read from right to left

parts.note: part means some, as in part of the cake

explanation.surface: Something set to catch intruders, with a party heading back to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a large spring trap once set on estates to snare poachers and other intruders.

clue.text: Ringing senator, confused about name

indicators.note: about means the muddled letters go round the abbreviation
confused means the letters of senator are muddled

explanation.surface: A puzzled senator's ears are ringing over a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' turns SENATOR into RESOATN, and 'about' wraps those letters around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is deep and echoing, so it rings on.

clue.text: Dismiss assembly and switch off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw out or expel
second meaning: the number of people who gather for an event
third meaning: to ... a light is to put it out

explanation.surface: An order to break up a meeting and put the lights out.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one phrase, read with or without its space.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the crowd attending an event; turn out also means expel or extinguish.

clue.text: Captivating orator to read out letters, having file of documents

parts.note: to spell a word is to say its letters one by one
a binder is a ring folder holding papers

explanation.surface: A gripping speaker reads out letters while holding a file of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spellbinder is a speaker who holds an audience enthralled, as if under a spell.

clue.text: Do nothing for stricken region

indicators.note: stricken means struck or wrecked, so the letters of region are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Officials do nothing to help a disaster-hit area.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to pay them no attention, doing nothing for them.

clue.text: Fish caught at busy centre

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hub is a busy central point of activity

explanation.surface: A fish is landed in a bustling spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Thought almost perfect

indicators.note: almost means the word for perfect stops just short of its end

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: Someone muses that something was very nearly perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: Pleasure seeker wandering into shed

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of into shed stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A fun-lover drifts aimlessly into a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for enjoyment, pursuing pleasure above all.

clue.text: Unit is reorganised without moving

indicators.note: reorganised means the letters of unit is are set in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A unit is restructured without relocating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a restructure that stays put, which is the meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original place, that is, not moved.

clue.text: Clever woman has underwear stored away?

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
something in a box is stored away

explanation.surface: A clever woman keeps her underwear packed away.
explanation.walkthrough: BRA followed by IN BOX: the bra is in the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is a very intelligent person, here a woman.

clue.text: To have a lot on their plate is healthy for politicians

definitions.text: To have a lot on their plate is healthy
definitions.meaning: first meaning: green vegetables, good to pile on a dinner plate
second meaning: members of a Green party

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot on their plate' sounds like being busy; literally it is vegetables on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens are leafy vegetables such as cabbage; the Greens are an environmentalist party.
